subject: Benchmarking takeover terms, bundle scenarios and next steps
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@shipyard.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring pricing match + migration package

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I run infrastructure & procurement for Shipyard. We're evaluating Redwood as a potential replacement for BrightScale. BrightScale has offered a multi-year lock with a sizable prepay and a migration allowance. Before we proceed, procurement wants to know if Redwood can match economics + provide an operational takeover plan (credits, onboarding assistance, license alignment).

High level:
- Current run-rate: ~3.2M tokens/month (mostly inference, mixed chat/generation).
- Current committed list: $420k/yr prepaid (BrightScale).
- Key asks: price parity or a migration credit, a simple SOW for onboarding, and a clear termination/rollback clause.

Can you share what a competitive match would look like and whether you have a standard migration credit structure? We'd like numbers we can take back to procurement by EOM.

Thanks —
Emma
Emma Park
Head of Infrastructure, Shipyard AI
emma@shipyard.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@shipyard.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring pricing match + migration package

Hi Emma — great to meet you. Thanks for the context. I'm looping in Karthik (commercial) and Vanessa (deployment lead) so we can put together an actionable bid. Preliminary thoughts below.

Short answer: yes, we can put forward a match-oriented offer, but we'll structure it to protect both sides while minimizing operational risk on cutover.

Proposed starter package (draft):
- Term: 12 months (pilot + committed tranche)
- Price: 10–20% below BrightScale list on comparable usage bands for first 12 months (tiered; details attached).
- Migration support: $75k onboarding credit + 2-week pilot (covering first ~100k tokens) and dedicated SE hours for runbook and KV cache handoff.
- Contract: Redwood standard term sheet (attached). We can add a 90-day rollback window with limited prorated credit if integration fails.

Attachments: takeover-econ-sheet.xlsx (breakout of tiers / suggested credits), redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf

Could you confirm two items so we can firm numbers: 1) expected 12-mo volume profile (monthly tokens), and 2) any data residency or KMS requirements? If you're comfortable, we'd aim to get an exec summary + term sheet back to you by EOW.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring pricing match + migration package

Looping through economics and fallback plan — re-quoting Soojin below for context.

> Proposed starter package (draft):
> - Term: 12 months (pilot + committed tranche)
> - Price: 10–20% below BrightScale list on comparable usage bands for first 12 months
> - Migration support: $75k onboarding credit + 2-week pilot (first ~100k tokens)

Reality check and options (quick bullets):
- Margin floor: hosted API at 20–25% discount is feasible for a 12-mo ramp if we keep network egress assumptions modest.
- For larger commitment (annual prepay >= $350k) we can do deeper pricing: 28–35% off list + $150k onboarding credit (buyout style).
- Alternate (risk-reducing): staged match — year 1: list-30% w/ $100k credit + canary windows; year 2: revert to standard volume pricing.

Packaging callouts (ops):
- Dedicated vs hosted: if they need Dedicated capacity, onboarding support doubles and the credit should be larger (we're suggesting $150k).
- SLA/credits: negotiate a 99.9% baseline; any outage credits beyond that need legal signoff.

Attached: SOW-draft.docx (initial scope + tasks).

Question for Vanessa: what does a 4-week Dedicated cutover look like operationally? If we're offering a $75k credit, is that sufficient to cover SE time + staging infra?

-Karthik
From: Emma Park <emma@shipyard.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@shipyard.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring pricing match + migration package

Soojin — thanks, that helps a lot.

A few quick notes from procurement & infra: we're leaning toward the staged match option (year 1 deeper discount + rollback guard). The two asks we'd need to take to legal this week are:
1) An exec summary (one page) that shows the delta vs BrightScale (price + credit + SLAs).
2) A redline-friendly term sheet (PDF) and an SOW we can attach to the PO.

We can share our monthly volume breakdown by EOD tomorrow. Also: no special KMS needs — standard cloud KMS is fine.

Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:00 PT to walk procurement through the numbers? If so, Jordan or Karthik can join as technical/commercial backup.

On the attachments: we'd like the SOW to include a cutover checklist and an ops rollback plan (1–2 pages).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emma
